body_markdown:
Bovensiepen, the company launched by the family[that started Alpina](https://www.hagerty.com/media/automotive-history/how-alpina-went-from-typewriters-to-high-octane-autobahn-burners/) , has revealed the second model it commissioned from Frank Stephenson Design. The new Bovensiepen Spider is a limited-edition, Z4-based roadster with sportier styling and more power.


Like[the 05 GT](https://www.hagerty.com/media/news/bovensiepen-05-gt-pricing-specs-pictures/) , the Spider looks a lot like the BMW it’s based on. The visual changes represent more of a facelift than a totally new look. They include a redesigned front splitter, a “Spider” logo behind each front wheel arch, deeper side skirts, and a wider rear diffuser with four oval exhaust outlets. Bovensiepen emblems and 20-inch wheels add a finishing touch to the exterior design.


Bovensiepen’s first convertible gets an evolution of the Z4’s turbocharged, 3.0-liter straight-six rated at 435 horsepower and 427 pound-feet of torque. For context, the engine posts figures of 382 and 369, respectively, in the regular-production car. Intake and exhaust modifications helped increase the output, and the Spider is capable of hitting 62 mph from a stop in 4.2 seconds on its way to a top speed of about 161 mph. If that’s not enough, buyers can unlock a 183-mph top speed with the optional Performance Pack.

Though software tweaks alone could likely add those 20 mph to the speedometer’s top end, Bovensiepen did make some mechanical changes, too. One of the features included in the Performance Pack is a new differential cover milled from aluminum with larger cooling fins. It reduces thermal load and allows the Z4 to reach the higher top speed. Underbody reinforcements are also part of the Performance Pack.


Newly tuned dampers and longer rear auxiliary springs further differentiate the Spider and the Z4 from the driver’s perspective.


Production of the Bovensiepen Spider is limited to 99 units globally. Pricing and availability haven’t been announced yet, but we’re guessing that they’ll all be built relatively soon because the G29-generation Z4[retired](https://www.hagerty.com/media/news/bmw-has-built-its-final-z4/) with[a Final Edition model](https://www.hagerty.com/media/news/bmw-z4-final-edition-specs-pictures-pricing/) earlier in 2026.
